messages:
Priya: hi all, new hire here. trying to demo streaming text generation against the hosted API but im getting intermittent 429s when I open ~6 browser tabs. is that expected for sandbox/hosted keys?
Dan: welcome! sandbox = smaller shared quotas. hosted org keys have higher limits but still enforce concurrency and tokens/min. 6 tabs could hit the concurrent-streams or requests/sec bucket.
Priya: how can i tell which bucket i'm hitting? headers? error body?
Rina: check the response headers on the 429. we surface info like remaining, reset timestamp, and retry-after. example:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1832101200
x-rw-retry-after: 2.5
{ "error": "rate_limited", "detail":"concurrent_streams" }
```
Dan: if the "detail" says concurrent_streams or requests_per_min you'll know. tokens/min will usually say tokens/min or similar.
Theo: practical tips: reuse a streaming connection where possible, multiplex logical sessions over one socket, or limit parallel demo tabs to 2-3. add exponential backoff on 429s: base 300ms, cap 4s, jitter.
Priya: can I request a temporary bump for a demo?
Rina: yes — for sandbox ask #devex with your email and the demo time window. for hosted ask your org admin or open a console quota request. devex usually approves small boosts for new hires. InfraBot: devex-boost-request created (ID: DB-887).
Priya: last q: do embedding requests share the same budget?
Dan: often embeddings count against the same tokens/min bucket unless your org has separate embedding quotas. look for x-rw-embed-* headers to confirm.
Priya: thanks — i'll tighten the demo to multiplex and ping devex for a short bump. :)
